items.title: Major Mountain Ranges & Plateaus of the World
items.body:
### Mountains and plateaus — the major landforms

**In one line**
Mountains (generally above **600 m**) are fold, block or volcanic; plateaus (flat-topped, generally over **300 m** above their surroundings) are intermontane, volcanic, erosional, dissected or continental — and each named range or plateau has a peak or resource to remember.

**The story — mountains**
- **Fold mountains** form when colliding plates fold the crust; mostly sedimentary and metamorphic rock. Young: **Himalayas**, Alps, Andes, Rockies, Atlas. Old: **Aravalli** (India), Appalachians, Urals.
- **Fault-block mountains** form by tension along faults — a steep front and gentle back: **Sierra Nevada** (USA), **Harz** (Germany).
- **Volcanic mountains**: Fuji, Vesuvius, Mauna Loa.

| Range | Length (km) | Highest peak (m) | Remember |
|---|---|---|---|
| Andes | 7,000 | **Aconcagua** 6,961 (Argentina) | **longest** continental range; 7 countries; **Lithium Triangle** (Argentina–Bolivia–Chile) |
| Rocky Mountains | 4,830 | **Mount Elbert** 4,401 (Colorado) | British Columbia to New Mexico |
| Great Dividing Range | 3,500 | **Kosciuszko** 2,228 | east Australia; source of the **Murray–Darling** |
| Atlas | 2,500 | **Toubkal** 4,167 (Morocco) | young fold; separates the **Sahara** from the coast |
| Urals | 2,500 | **Narodnaya** 1,894 | old fold; **Europe–Asia boundary**; mineral base of Russia |
| Appalachians | 2,414 | **Mitchell** 2,037 | very old fold (~480 million years) |
| Himalayas | 2,400 | **Everest** 8,849 | young fold (~50 million years); **"Water Tower of Asia"** |
| Altai | 2,000 | **Belukha** 4,506 | Russia–Mongolia–China–Kazakhstan |
| Scandinavian (Scandes) | 1,700 | **Galdhopiggen** 2,469 (Norway) | |
| Alps | 1,200 | **Mont Blanc** 4,809 (France–Italy) | young fold (~30 million years); 8 countries |
| Drakensberg | 1,125 | **Thabana Ntlenyana** 3,482 (Lesotho) | South Africa |

The highest volcano, **Ojos del Salado** (6,893 m), is in the Andes.

**The story — plateaus**

| Type | Example |
|---|---|
| Intermontane (between ranges) | **Tibetan Plateau** — world's **largest and highest**, the "**Roof of the World**"; Columbia Plateau |
| Volcanic (lava) | **Deccan Plateau** (India's largest plateau, between the Western and Eastern Ghats); **Columbia–Snake** (USA) |
| Erosional | **Colorado Plateau** (Grand Canyon) |
| Dissected | **Ozark Plateau** (USA) |
| Continental | **Katanga Plateau** (Africa) |

**Named plateaus and resources**

| Plateau | Fact |
|---|---|
| Kimberley (Australia) | **kimberlite** — diamond-bearing rock |
| Katanga (DR Congo) | **copper and uranium** |
| Laurentian (Canada) | the **Canadian Shield**; Precambrian rocks; iron ore |
| Mexican (Altiplano) | "**Mineral Store**"; world's largest **silver** mine (Chihuahua) |
| Altiplano (Peru–Bolivia) | **tin** |
| Patagonian (Argentina) | rain-shadow semi-desert; **sheep rearing** |
| Anatolian (Turkey, Asia Minor) | **Angora goats** (mohair wool) |
| Massif Central (France) | faulting; **grapes** |
| Iberian (Spain) | high-quality **iron** |
| Loess / Huangtu (China) | the **most erodible soil** in the world |
| Pothohar (Pakistan) | between the **Jhelum** (east) and **Indus** (west); **Salt Range** to the south |
| Mascarene (Indian Ocean) | undersea **granite** remnant of Gondwana; second to the **Kerguelen** |
| Ahaggar / Hoggar (Algeria) | volcanic basalt in the Sahara |
| Bavarian (Germany) | the **Alpine Foreland**, shaped by ice ages |
| Chota Nagpur (India) | India's **mineral heartland** |

**Don't confuse**
Andes = longest range; Himalayas = highest. Tibetan = highest plateau; Deccan = largest in India.

**TL;DR**
- Mountains > 600 m; fold (Himalayas young, Aravalli old), block (Sierra Nevada, Harz), volcanic (Fuji).
- Andes 7,000 km (Aconcagua); Rockies (Elbert); Alps (Mont Blanc); Urals (Europe–Asia, Narodnaya); Atlas (Toubkal); Drakensberg (Lesotho).
- Plateaus > 300 m; Tibetan largest and highest; Deccan volcanic; Colorado erosional.
- Kimberley diamonds, Katanga copper–uranium, Mexican silver, Altiplano tin, Anatolia Angora goats, Laurentian = Canadian Shield.
keyPoints: Mountains generally rise above 600 m; fold (Himalayas young, Aravalli old), fault-block (Sierra Nevada, Harz), volcanic.
Andes (7,000 km) is the longest continental range — Aconcagua 6,961 m; Lithium Triangle.
Rockies — Mount Elbert; Great Dividing Range — Kosciuszko (Murray–Darling source); Atlas — Toubkal; Urals — Narodnaya (Europe–Asia boundary).
Appalachians very old (~480 million years) — Mount Mitchell; Alps young (~30 million years) — Mont Blanc 4,809 m.
Himalayas — Everest 8,849 m, the "Water Tower of Asia"; Drakensberg — Thabana Ntlenyana (Lesotho); Altai — Belukha.
Plateaus rise over 300 m; types: intermontane (Tibetan, Roof of the World), volcanic (Deccan), erosional (Colorado), dissected (Ozark), continental (Katanga).
Kimberley — kimberlite diamonds; Katanga — copper and uranium; Laurentian = Canadian Shield; Mexican — silver (Chihuahua); Altiplano — tin.
Patagonian — sheep; Anatolian — Angora goats; Massif Central — grapes; Loess/Huangtu — most erodible soil; Pothohar — between Jhelum and Indus.

items.title: For Mains — Internal Structure & Major Landforms
items.body:
### For Mains — how this topic is framed in Paper-2

Mains (GS Paper-2, Section on Geography of India & AP — clauses **M2-11** physical features & resources and **M2-15** environmental geography/natural hazards & disaster management) rarely wants a plain list of landforms. It wants you to **link process to pattern to policy** — how tectonics and geomorphic agents create India's and AP's relief, resources and hazards, and what should be done about the hazards.

**Dimensions Mains asks (use as an answer skeleton)**

| Dimension | What to write |
|---|---|
| Process | plate tectonics, endogenic vs exogenic forces, rock/landform genesis |
| Pattern | distribution of mountains, plateaus, deltas, seismic zones in India/AP |
| Resources | rock-system minerals (coal, oil, metals), deltaic soils, groundwater |
| Hazards | earthquakes (Zone V), volcanism, landslides, coastal/flood risk |
| Impact | on agriculture, settlement, infrastructure, livelihoods |
| Way forward | seismic micro-zonation, building codes, disaster preparedness |

**Facts, reports and schemes to quote**
- **~59% of India** is prone to moderate-to-severe earthquakes; the Himalaya, NE, Kutch and Andaman lie in **Seismic Zone V**.
- **Bureau of Indian Standards IS 1893** seismic building code; **National Disaster Management Act, 2005** and **NDMA** guidelines.
- **Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction (2015–2030)** — the global benchmark India has adopted.
- **Gondwana ~98% of coal**; **Tertiary** rocks = petroleum; **Krishna-Godavari basin** gas — a direct AP resource.
- **Deccan Traps** (~60 mya) and the ancient **Eastern Ghats** as peninsular structural features.

**The AP angle**
Andhra Pradesh sits on the **stable Deccan/peninsular block** with the old **Eastern Ghats**, so it is low-seismicity — but its long **coast is cyclone- and tsunami-exposed** (2004 Indian Ocean tsunami), and the fertile **Godavari and Krishna arcuate deltas** are both its agricultural heartland and its flood-risk zone. Barren Island volcanism lies offshore in the Union Territory waters nearby.

**Use in answers**
- **Example to cite**: contrast the rising, quake-prone Himalaya (convergent margin) with AP's stable deltaic coast to show the plate-interior-versus-margin idea.
- **Diagram idea**: a labelled section of a convergent boundary (subduction → trench → fold mountain → volcano), or India's four-zone seismic map.
- **Quote**: frame disaster policy as a shift 'from relief-centric to prevention-centric' (DM Act, 2005 spirit).

**TL;DR**
- Answer process → pattern → resources → hazards → impact → way forward, not a landform list.
- Anchor with Zone V (~59% at risk), IS 1893, DM Act 2005, NDMA and the Sendai Framework.
- Use AP's stable block + deltaic coast as the running example and a boundary cross-section as the diagram.
keyPoints: Frame M2-11/M2-15 answers as process → pattern → resources → hazards → impact → way forward.
Quote ~59% of India in moderate-severe seismic risk; Zone V = Himalaya, NE, Kutch, Andaman.
Cite IS 1893 building code, Disaster Management Act 2005, NDMA, and the Sendai Framework (2015–2030).
AP angle: stable Deccan/Eastern Ghats block (low seismicity) but cyclone/tsunami-exposed Godavari–Krishna deltaic coast.
Diagram idea: convergent-boundary cross-section or India's seismic-zone map; contrast Himalaya (margin) with AP (interior).
